correctness.rationale: For even k, RC orbit counts (2^k+2^(k/2))/2 give 3,10,36 at k=2,4,6. Explicit witnesses cover the first two bounds. The 5 high-potential and 5 RC-low-potential states produce a 0..3 nonnegative six-mer cost constant on RC classes. An independent enumeration of all 64 six-mers verified eight fixed words, sum 18 of fixed-word weights, and total 41 when counting all 36 RC classes once. Telescoping along any linear word yields total cost at most L+2 for L six-mer windows, forcing L>=39. Independently evaluated the explicit 44-bit word and found all 36 classes among its 39 windows, with precisely three classes appearing twice and zero weights on those repeats. This is a universal lower bound plus exact witness, not inference from brute-force search over all strings.
residual_risks: Finite exhaustive verification is restricted to its specified domain.

value.rationale: A compact nonnegative potential certificate resolves the first binary even-order deficit for a basic de Bruijn/reverse-complement covering problem. The precise value 44 and three-window obstruction are natural length and symmetry invariants, useful independently of the established general polynomial algorithm; the displayed dual proof explains why orbit counting fails.
residual_risks: The value is finite or parameter-specific and should not be promoted as an all-parameter theorem.

final_claim: For linear binary reverse-complement covering strings, minimum lengths at k=2,4,6 are 4,13,44; the first even-order orbit lower-bound failure occurs at k=6 with three surplus windows.
limitations: Binary alphabet and linear windows at k=2,4,6 only; no result for four-letter DNA or all even orders.
